judgment.preOpenPreflightReason: diagnosis, reproduction, and the initial fix ran interleaved with a long multi-hour session covering unrelated conversation and async waits on webhook events/background subagents — no clean timestamp separates preflight from the rest of the session, so recorded as unknown rather than estimated.
judgment.breakersFired: Round 5's rising-finding-count stopping rule (working-modes.md's review-loop stopping rule — findings went 3/2/2/2/3 round over round; the round-5 rise triggered a pause-and-check-in with David before requesting round 6, rather than auto-continuing). The any-decline Opus-subagent-challenge trigger fired four times: R1's pronoun-resolver finding and R2's CDN-cache finding were both findings I initially leaned toward declining, and both challenges overturned that instinct — the pronoun finding partially (fix ze/xe, defer the rest) and the CDN finding fully (fixed outright, a real lever I'd missed). R1's legacy-token finding and R2's identity-drift finding were both findings where the challenge was dispatched and came back CONFIRMING the decline was correct, in the identity-drift case with added nuance (broadened the tracking issue from one trigger to three). Round 4's swept-class-recurrence trigger (a finding recurring from an earlier round should route to a fresh Opus-subagent challenge before declining) did NOT run through a fresh subagent that round — I declined it directly, citing David's own already-stated explicit decision as sufficient grounds. Recording this as a partial/adapted application of that specific rule, not a clean firing of it — distinct from the four Opus challenges that did fire cleanly in R1-R2.

notes: Self-authored at loop close, 2026-08-10 (Claude Code, Sonnet). Cause classification: R1's 3 findings (pronoun resolver gap, legacy-token gap, my own UAT doc's inaccurate claim) are new_ground — none had an earlier round-of-this-loop fix to be caused by (round 1 reviews the original submission). R2's 2 findings (picture-vs-caption identity drift confirmed via git blame as pre-existing; CDN edge-cache staleness rooted in the original MEME_RENDER_VERSION bump) are both new_ground — pre-existing defects exposed by, not caused by, the loop's own fixes. R3's deploy-ordering hazard is propagation (round 2's Worker-versioning mechanism is the reason it exists at all); R3's Zazzle-export cache gap is new_ground (pre-existing property of /api/storage/objects/*'s cache header + the fixed export path, unrelated to round 2's fix, exposed by round 1's render fix making a corrected re-export meaningful for the first time). R4's misplaced deploy-order warning is wrong_fix (round 3's fix didn't resolve what it claimed — an operator following the actual runbook still wouldn't see it); R4's custom-pronoun-parity recurrence is reRaised (restates R1's finding with no new information, no failed fix attempt between them — R1 declined it, never attempted it). R5's three findings are: verification-command cache blind spot — wrong_fix (the command was introduced in round 3 specifically to close the ordering-hazard concern, and didn't fully close it); constant-drift-with-no-guard and stale architecture docs — both propagation (neither defect is possible without round 2's and round 3's respective fixes existing). 0 invalid: every finding investigated turned out real, including two (R1's pronoun gap, R2's identity-drift) I initially leaned toward declining and only confirmed as fix-worthy or correctly-scoped after dispatching an adversarial Opus-subagent challenge against my own reasoning.
